passages.text: When Solomon had finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was the king of Israel.
Solomon finished praying.
Fire came down from heaven.
The fire consumed the burnt offering.
The fire consumed the sacrifices.
The glory of the LORD filled the temple.
passages.original: וּכְכַלּ֤וֹת שְׁלֹמֹה֙ לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֔ל וְהָאֵ֗שׁ יָֽרְדָה֙ מֵֽהַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַתֹּ֥אכַל הָעֹלָ֖ה וְהַזְּבָחִ֑ים וּכְב֥וֹד יְהוָ֖ה מָלֵ֥א אֶת־ הַבָּֽיִת׃

passages.text: The priests were unable to enter the house of the LORD, because the glory of the LORD had filled it.
passages.sermon:
The priests served God in the temple.
The priests could not enter the house of the LORD.
The glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.
The glory of the LORD made it impossible for the priests to go inside.
passages.original: וְלֹ֤א יָֽכְלוּ֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים לָב֖וֹא אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה כִּֽי־ מָלֵ֥א כְבוֹד־ יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: When all the Israelites saw the fire coming down and the glory of the LORD above the temple, they bowed down on the pavement with their faces to the ground, and they worshiped and gave thanks to the LORD: “For He is good; His loving devotion endures forever.”
passages.sermon:
All the Israelites saw the fire come down from heaven.
They saw the glory of the LORD above the temple.
The Israelites bowed down with their faces to the ground.
They bowed on the pavement.
They worshiped the LORD.
They gave thanks to the LORD.
They said, “He is good.”
They said, “His loving devotion endures forever.”
passages.original: וְכֹ֣ל׀ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל רֹאִים֙ בְּרֶ֣דֶת הָאֵ֔שׁ וּכְב֥וֹד יְהוָ֖ה עַל־ הַבָּ֑יִת וַיִּכְרְעוּ֩ אַפַּ֨יִם אַ֤רְצָה עַל־ הָרִֽצְפָה֙ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּֽחֲו֔וּ וְהוֹד֤וֹת לַיהוָה֙ כִּ֣י ט֔וֹב כִּ֥י לְעוֹלָ֖ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the LORD.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon led the people of Israel.
All the people of Israel joined him.
They offered sacrifices.
They offered these sacrifices before the LORD.
passages.original: וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְכָל־ הָעָ֑ם זֹבְחִ֥ים זֶ֖בַח לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: And King Solomon offered a sacrifice of 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep. So the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was the ruler of Israel.
King Solomon offered a sacrifice to the LORD.
He sacrificed 22,000 oxen.
He also sacrificed 120,000 sheep.
King Solomon and all the people dedicated the house of God.
passages.original: וַיִּזְבַּ֞ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֮ אֶת־ זֶ֣בַח הַבָּקָ֗ר עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וּשְׁנַ֙יִם֙ אֶ֔לֶף וְצֹ֕אן מֵאָ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים אָ֑לֶף וַֽיַּחְנְכוּ֙ אֶת־ בֵּ֣ית הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְכָל־ הָעָֽם׃

passages.text: The priests stood at their posts, as did the Levites with the musical instruments of the LORD, which King David had made for giving thanks to the LORD and with which David had offered praise, saying, “For His loving devotion endures forever.” Across from the Levites, the priests sounded trumpets, and all the Israelites were standing.
passages.sermon:
The priests stood at their posts.
The Levites also stood at their posts.
The Levites held the musical instruments of the LORD.
King David had made these instruments.
David made them to give thanks to the LORD.
David used them to offer praise.
David said, “For His loving devotion endures forever.”
The priests stood across from the Levites.
The priests sounded trumpets.
All the Israelites were standing.
passages.original: וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֞ים עַל־ מִשְׁמְרוֹתָ֣ם עֹמְדִ֗ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֞ם בִּכְלֵי־ שִׁ֤יר יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה דָּוִ֣יד הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ לְהֹד֤וֹת לַיהוָה֙ כִּֽי־ לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּ֔וֹ בְּהַלֵּ֥ל דָּוִ֖יד בְּיָדָ֑ם וְהַכֹּהֲנִים֙ מַחֲצֹצְרִים נֶגְדָּ֔ם וְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עֹמְדִֽים׃ס

passages.text: Then Solomon consecrated the middle of the courtyard in front of the house of the LORD, and there he offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, since the bronze altar he had made could not contain all these offerings.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon consecrated the middle area of the courtyard.
This courtyard stood in front of the house of the LORD.
Solomon offered burnt offerings there.
He also offered the fat from the peace offerings there.
The bronze altar that Solomon had made was not large enough.
It could not hold all the burnt offerings.
It could not hold all the grain offerings.
It could not hold all the fat portions.
passages.original: וַיְקַדֵּ֣שׁ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה אֶת־ תּ֤וֹךְ הֶֽחָצֵר֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י בֵית־ יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי־ עָ֤שָׂה שָׁם֙ הָֽעֹל֔וֹת וְאֵ֖ת חֶלְבֵ֣י הַשְּׁלָמִ֑ים כִּֽי־ מִזְבַּ֤ח הַנְּחֹ֙שֶׁת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֣ה שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה לֹ֣א יָכ֗וֹל לְהָכִ֛יל אֶת־ הָעֹלָ֥ה וְאֶת־ הַמִּנְחָ֖ה וְאֶת־ הַחֲלָבִֽים׃

passages.text: So at that time Solomon and all Israel with him—a very great assembly of people from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt—kept the feast for seven days.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king of Israel.
At that time, Solomon kept the feast.
He celebrated the feast for seven days.
All Israel was with Solomon.
A very large assembly of people joined him.
The people came from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה אֶת־ הֶ֠חָג בָּעֵ֨ת הַהִ֜יא שִׁבְעַ֤ת יָמִים֙ וְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עִמּ֔וֹ קָהָ֖ל גָּד֣וֹל מְאֹ֑ד מִלְּב֥וֹא חֲמָ֖ת עַד־ נַ֥חַל מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: On the eighth day they held a solemn assembly, for the dedication of the altar had lasted seven days, and the feast seven days more.
passages.sermon:
Solomon led the people of Israel.
On the eighth day, the people gathered for a solemn assembly.
They had dedicated the altar for seven days.
They had also celebrated the feast for seven days.
passages.original: וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֛וּ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִ֖י עֲצָ֑רֶת כִּ֣י׀ חֲנֻכַּ֣ת הַמִּזְבֵּ֗חַ עָשׂוּ֙ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים וְהֶחָ֖ג שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃

passages.text: On the twenty-third day of the seventh month, Solomon sent the people away to their homes, joyful and glad of heart for the good things that the LORD had done for David, for Solomon, and for His people Israel.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was the king of Israel.
On the twenty-third day of the seventh month, Solomon sent the people to their homes.
The people felt joy.
The people had glad hearts.
The LORD had done good things for David.
The LORD had done good things for Solomon.
The LORD had done good things for His people Israel.
passages.original: וּבְי֨וֹם עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י שִׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־ הָעָ֖ם לְאָהֳלֵיהֶ֑ם שְׂמֵחִים֙ וְט֣וֹבֵי לֵ֔ב עַל־ הַטּוֹבָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לְדָוִ֣יד וְלִשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When Solomon had finished the house of the LORD and the royal palace, successfully carrying out all that was in his heart to do for the house of the LORD and for his own palace, the LORD appeared to him at night and said to him: “I have heard your prayer and have chosen this place for Myself as a house of sacrifice.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king of Israel.
Solomon finished building the house of the LORD.
Solomon finished building the royal palace.
Solomon did everything he wanted to do for the house of the LORD.
Solomon did everything he wanted to do for his own palace.
Solomon succeeded in all these things.
The LORD appeared to Solomon at night.
The LORD spoke to Solomon.
The LORD said, “I have heard your prayer.
I have chosen this place for Myself.
This place will be a house of sacrifice for Me.”
passages.original: וַיְכַ֧ל שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה אֶת־ בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה וְאֶת־ בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־ הַבָּ֜א עַל־ לֵ֣ב שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לַעֲשׂ֧וֹת בְּבֵית־ יְהוָ֛ה וּבְבֵית֖וֹ הִצְלִֽיחַ׃פ וַיֵּרָ֧א יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בַּלָּ֑יְלָה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי֙ אֶת־ תְּפִלָּתֶ֔ךָ וּבָחַ֜רְתִּי בַּמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֛ה לִ֖י לְבֵ֥ית זָֽבַח׃

passages.text: If I close the sky so there is no rain, or if I command the locust to devour the land, or if I send a plague among My people, and if My people who are called by My name humble themselves and pray and seek My face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, forgive their sin, and heal their land.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Solomon.
God has power over nature and people.
God may close the sky.
No rain will fall if God closes the sky.
God may command locusts.
The locusts will eat the land if God commands them.
God may send a plague among His people.
God’s people are called by His name.
If God’s people humble themselves, God will notice.
If God’s people pray, God will listen.
If God’s people seek God’s face, God will respond.
If God’s people turn from their wicked ways, God will see.
God will hear from heaven.
God will forgive their sin.
God will heal their land.
passages.original: הֵ֣ן אֶֽעֱצֹ֤ר הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ וְלֹֽא־ יִהְיֶ֣ה מָטָ֔ר וְהֵן־ אֲצַוֶּ֥ה עַל־ חָגָ֖ב לֶאֱכ֣וֹל הָאָ֑רֶץ וְאִם־ אֲשַׁלַּ֥ח דֶּ֖בֶר בְּעַמִּֽי׃ וְיִכָּנְע֨וּ עַמִּ֜י אֲשֶׁ֧ר נִֽקְרָא־ שְׁמִ֣י עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם וְיִֽתְפַּֽלְלוּ֙ וִֽיבַקְשׁ֣וּ פָנַ֔י וְיָשֻׁ֖בוּ מִדַּרְכֵיהֶ֣ם הָרָעִ֑ים וַאֲנִי֙ אֶשְׁמַ֣ע מִן־ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְאֶסְלַח֙ לְחַטָּאתָ֔ם וְאֶרְפָּ֖א אֶת־ אַרְצָֽם׃

passages.text: Now My eyes will be open and My ears attentive to the prayers offered in this place.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Solomon at night.
God had chosen the temple in Jerusalem as His house of sacrifice.
God said, "Now My eyes will be open."
God said, "My ears will listen carefully."
God will pay attention to the prayers made in this temple.
passages.original: עַתָּ֗ה עֵינַי֙ יִהְי֣וּ פְתֻח֔וֹת וְאָזְנַ֖י קַשֻּׁב֑וֹת לִתְפִלַּ֖ת הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: For I have now chosen and consecrated this temple so that My Name may be there forever. My eyes and My heart will be there for all time.
passages.sermon:
God speaks in this passage.
God has chosen this temple.
God has made this temple holy.
God wants His Name to be in this temple forever.
God will keep His eyes on this temple always.
God’s heart will be with this temple for all time.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה בָּחַ֤רְתִּי וְהִקְדַּ֙שְׁתִּי֙ אֶת־ הַבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּ֔ה לִהְיוֹת־ שְׁמִ֥י שָׁ֖ם עַד־ עוֹלָ֑ם וְהָי֨וּ עֵינַ֧י וְלִבִּ֛י שָׁ֖ם כָּל־ הַיָּמִֽים׃

passages.text: And as for you, if you walk before Me as your father David walked, doing all I have commanded you, and if you keep My statutes and ordinances, then I will establish your royal throne, as I covenanted with your father David when I said, ‘You will never fail to have a man to rule over Israel.’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Solomon, the king of Israel.
God gave Solomon a command.
God said, "If you walk before Me faithfully, as your father David did, I will bless you."
God told Solomon to do everything He commanded.
God told Solomon to keep His statutes and ordinances.
God promised to establish Solomon’s royal throne if he obeyed.
God made a covenant with David, Solomon’s father.
God said to David, "You will always have a descendant to rule over Israel."
God promised to keep this covenant with Solomon if Solomon obeyed.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֞ה אִם־ תֵּלֵ֣ךְ לְפָנַ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר הָלַךְ֙ דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֔יךָ וְלַעֲשׂ֕וֹת כְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֑יךָ וְחֻקַּ֥י וּמִשְׁפָּטַ֖י תִּשְׁמֽוֹר׃ וַהֲקִ֣ימוֹתִ֔י אֵ֖ת כִּסֵּ֣א מַלְכוּתֶ֑ךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּרַ֗תִּי לְדָוִ֤יד אָבִ֙יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹֽא־ יִכָּרֵ֤ת לְךָ֙ אִ֔ישׁ מוֹשֵׁ֖ל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: But if you turn away and forsake the statutes and commandments I have set before you, and if you go off to serve and worship other gods, then I will uproot Israel from the soil I have given them, and I will banish from My presence this temple I have sanctified for My Name. I will make it an object of scorn and ridicule among all the peoples.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Israel.
God gave Israel statutes and commandments.
God set these laws before Israel.
God warned Israel about turning away.
If you turn away from God’s laws,
If you abandon the commandments God gave you,
If you go and serve other gods,
If you bow down to them,
Then God will act.
God will uproot you from the land He gave you.
God will remove you from your soil.
God chose and sanctified the temple for His Name.
God will cast this temple out of His presence.
God will make the temple a proverb among all peoples.
God will make the temple a subject of ridicule among all nations.
passages.original: וְאִם־ תְּשׁוּב֣וּן אַתֶּ֔ם וַעֲזַבְתֶּם֙ חֻקּוֹתַ֣י וּמִצְוֺתַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לִפְנֵיכֶ֑ם וַהֲלַכְתֶּ֗ם וַעֲבַדְתֶּם֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֖ם לָהֶֽם׃ וּנְתַשְׁתִּ֗ים מֵעַ֤ל אַדְמָתִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תִּי לָהֶ֔ם וְאֶת־ הַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִקְדַּ֣שְׁתִּי לִשְׁמִ֔י אַשְׁלִ֖יךְ מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑י וְאֶתְּנֶ֛נּוּ לְמָשָׁ֥ל וְלִשְׁנִינָ֖ה בְּכָל־ הָעַמִּֽים׃

passages.text: And when this temple has become a heap of rubble, all who pass by it will be appalled and say, ‘Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?’
passages.sermon:
This house was once exalted.
This house refers to the temple in Jerusalem.
God had chosen and sanctified this temple for His Name.
People from many nations recognized its greatness.
But now the temple lies in ruins.
Everyone who passes by will be shocked.
They will see the destruction.
They will feel horror and amazement.
They will ask a question.
They will say, "Why did the LORD do this?"
They will ask, "Why did the LORD do this to this land?"
They will ask, "Why did the LORD do this to this temple?"
passages.original: וְהַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה עֶלְי֔וֹן לְכָל־ עֹבֵ֥ר עָלָ֖יו יִשֹּׁ֑ם וְאָמַ֗ר בַּמֶּ֨ה עָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ כָּ֔כָה לָאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּ֖את וְלַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: And others will answer, ‘Because they have forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and have embraced other gods, worshiping and serving them—because of this, He has brought all this disaster upon them.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel left the LORD.
The LORD is the God of their fathers.
The LORD brought their fathers out of Egypt.
The people of Israel chose other gods.
They worshiped these other gods.
They served these other gods.
Because of this, the LORD brought disaster on them.
passages.original: וְאָמְר֗וּ עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָֽזְב֜וּ אֶת־ יְהוָ֣ה׀ אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתֵיהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר הוֹצִיאָם֮ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַיִם֒ וַֽיַּחֲזִ֙יקוּ֙ בֵּאלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲו֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם וַיַּֽעַבְד֑וּם עַל־ כֵּן֙ הֵבִ֣יא עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הָרָעָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃פ
